_comment: Grey Baltic, out of season. The temptation with a beach is to make it a holiday; this one is deliberately not. Flat overcast, nobody else, everything packed away -- a family walk in October, which is the version people actually have on tape.
label: Baltic beach, out of season

prompt._comment: Strandkorb -- the roofed wicker beach chair -- is the detail that says Baltic rather than any grey coast in Europe. Turned away from the water is what says out of season.
prompt.scene: a wide grey Baltic beach out of season, wet packed sand, a line of roofed wicker beach chairs turned away from the water, marram grass on the dune behind, a groyne of black timber posts running out into the sea
prompt.light: flat overcast with no shadow at all, the water and the sky nearly the same grey, the sand slightly brighter than both
prompt.lens: wide and low with a lot of sky, the horizon almost straight across the frame
prompt.framing: waist-up against the empty sand, the groyne running away over one shoulder
prompt._moment: What is HAPPENING, not what is in frame. A brief with no action in it is a portrait brief, and the model answers it with a portrait -- squared to the camera, arms hanging, waiting. Somebody caught halfway through something ordinary is what a real snapshot looks like.
prompt.moment: walking back up the sand and only just noticing the camera, one arm still out for balance
prompt.eraProps: roofed wicker beach chairs, a striped canvas wind-break, a metal thermos flask, a fold-out paper map weighted down with a stone

motionHint: the water moves in slow flat lines up the sand, the marram grass bends steadily, and the canvas of the wind-break snaps

lookOverride._comment: The coldest and flattest thing in the menu. Saturation well down, warmth backed almost out (remember bm negative = yellow, so raising cbBlueMid towards zero cools it), halation nearly off because a flat overcast sky has no specular highlight to halate, and the least grain of any preset because there is nothing here for it to hide in.

ambience._comment: Surf and onshore wind. The swell is the waves: 0.18 Hz is about one every five and a half seconds, which is what the preset means by "slow flat lines up the sand". Lowpassed hard because a camcorder mic in wind has no top end left.
